context:
Goal: no session builds, serves or edits inside another checkout by mistake.
Problem (risk): on Oct 28 you dropped banchi's own tree check because the shared other-checkout rule covers it, but a test shows it does not, so merging #1003 as built opens a gap that only your word can accept or close.
Based on (measured): the third reviewer's tests on #1003: with it, a cd into another checkout followed by npm run build passes, and so do make up, npm install, touch, mkdir and a bare cd; main refuses all of these today.
Based on (ruling): your Oct 28 ruling to skip banchi's own tree check, since the shared rule covers it.
Departs from: main (banchi's own check refuses a cd into another checkout) — option B moves that refusal into the shared guard for every repo; option A keeps it in banchi only.
holds: banchi PR #1003 is held until you pick.

options.gain: Closes the gap in banchi now.
options.how: banchi keeps refusing a cd into another checkout on Claude Code's shell commands; the rest of its tree check goes, as you ruled.
options.label: Keep only banchi's cd refusal
options.lose: One more banchi-only rule, and other repos stay open.

options.gain: One rule covers every repo, and your Oct 28 intent holds.
options.how: The shared guard refuses a cd into another checkout in every repo; then #1003 merges.
options.label: The shared guard refuses it for every repo

options.how: #1003 merges now, and these acts are named as known limits.
options.label: Accept the gap
options.lose: Building in another checkout by mistake can happen in banchi again.

ref: banchi PR #1003 (step c174, banchi skips its own tree check)
reply: Pick b taken (saved Nov 1 17:25 CST). The banchi lane for step c174 builds it.
title: Your Oct 28 ruling dropped banchi's tree check because the shared rule covers it, but it does not: where should the fix live?
why: A gap one repo finds in the shared rules gets fixed in the shared rules, once, for every repo.
